notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen last game. Connor Brown takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Brenden Dillon is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Kovacevic and Chisholm.
Anthony Mantha is out and missed their last game.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Josh Morrissey is on injured reserve (wrist injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Mario Ferraro has taken his spot beside Dylan DeMelo. That pair has had 54% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 116:45 together, down from 61% with Morrissey.
Elias Salomonsson is away for personal reasons and has missed the last 2 games. Dylan DeMelo has taken his spot beside Mario Ferraro.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Devils go in second in the Metropolitan with 26 points, the Jets sixth in the Central with 17 points.

WPG.head: The Jets face a real test
WPG.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. The Jets’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

NJD.head: Advantage, the Devils
NJD.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. The Jets’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Mercer meets his old team
paras: The Jets have won three straight. The Devils have won five straight, the last a 4-0 rout of Toronto, and they’re rolling. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 22nd).

The Devils draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and rarely throw hits (2nd lowest). They also throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd), so the Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets. On the other side, the Jets ice the puck less than anyone (1st), create chances on the penalty kill (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (3rd).

Jack Hughes (9 G / 16 A / 25 P in 18 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Jesper Bratt (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (13 G / 6 A / 19 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring. Mark Scheifele (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games.

Stuart Skinner (6-4-3 / .883 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Winnipeg. New Jersey has two options in net: Connor Hellebuyck (5-0-0 / .913 SV% in 5 GS) and Jake Allen (6-3-0 / .881 SV% in 9 GS). Hellebuyck has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Sunday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Devils usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
